The Passive of Modal Verbs, Must and Should
Must and Should in passive voice are used to express obligations and suggestions from an unknown or non-relevant performer.

Must in passive voice has three uses: 

  • To express that something has to be done because it’s compulsory.
  • To talk about something that is likely to be like that because of a logical explanation or real evidence.
  • To express urgent or strong advice.

 For example: 

The contract must be signed after reading it all.

Should is used: 

  • To express what we think is right or wrong.
  • To express advice or suggestions.

For example:

The provisions should be explained in detail.

This is the grammatical structure to use must and should in the passive voice:

 Subject + Must/Should + Be + Past participle verb + Complement
Response times from the service provider must be stated clearly as well so as to avoid breakdowns.
The vendor must offer a cure period that should be measured in days.
When customers want to acquire software as a service, the standard SLA contract must be given right away, and they should start negotiating afterwards.
A service-level agreement contains some metrics that need to be specified when accessing the service.

A service-level agreement (SLA) is a contract that a service provider and a customer meet when getting cloud services.

Some metrics that SLAs may specify are: 

  • Specific standards to be sporadically compared.
  • Application time.
  • Changes notifications.
  • Help assistance for different problems.
  • Statistics use provided.

Rodolph, a cloud service provider, talks about a SaaS contract with the CEO of a company.
Instructions: Read the dialogue and select the correct answer.

CEO: How can you assure that our data is going to be available when we need it?
Rodolph: Do not worry, here in the document, all the information related to the service level agreement must be explained.
CEO: What is the service level agreement about?
Rodolph: It is a commitment, a guarantee, in which all the quality of the cloud service is specified. Regarding availability of data, there is something called fix times, which assures our customers that any problem must be fixed within a period of time depending on the severity of the situation. For example, if there is a minor problem, we can fix it within an hour or so.
CEO: Does it guarantee that there is not going to be any breakdown in the service?
Rodolph: Yes. We are not used to having breakdowns, but if there is a breach, you can have a cure period. This period must be specified in the contract; so, we have to discuss that matter.
CEO: I'm relieved because otherwise, we will have to rush in order to hire another provider, and that must be informed to all the company employees.
Rodolph: All this information must be included in the contract, and the negotiations should be made right after the document is ready.
What must be explained in the contract?

images.text: Software as a Service (SaaS), commonly called cloud service, allows companies to store data and applications over the Internet. To do so, companies and service providers need to sign a SaaS contract, in which a definitive service guarantee must be provided. This guarantee is called Service Level Agreement (SLA), and some provisions, such as availability of data, must be included on it. An SLA obligates providers to know the standard of availability or uptime as a percentage of the time. Response times from the service provider must be stated clearly as well so as to avoid breakdowns.

Besides, fix times should be agreed upon a period of time according to the severity of the problem. Good thing is that vendors are always willing to fix issues immediately, especially if others are experiencing the same situation. Plus, if the vendor doesn’t fulfill his obligations, the customer can call for a contract termination due to breach; as a remedy, the vendor must offer a cure period that should be measured in days; otherwise, the customer will have to rush to get a new provider. When customers want to acquire software as a service, the standard SLA contract must be given right away, and they should start negotiating afterwards.

Customers must read the document carefully because, like any other contract, there are legal consequences if the provisions are not clear. On the contract, the vendor must warrant a security plan to protect customers’ data and applications. Also, any security breach must be notified, no matter how reluctant the providers are. Other provisions include privacy, export, and jurisdictional issues that show up out of the location of the cloud service, which could trigger export laws. To conclude, the SaaS contract must be checked and negotiated in detail by both parties, service providers and customers, to avoid misapprehensions.
